problem.title: Prescription Refill Retention Rates
problem.prompt: You are analyzing prescription refill behavior. Write a query that computes the refill rate at 30, 60, and 90 days across all patients. A patient's first fill is their earliest fill_date; a refill is any subsequent fill (strict greater-than) within the time window. Each patient counts at most once in each window, even if they refilled multiple times. Return a single row with three columns: refill_rate_30d, refill_rate_60d, refill_rate_90d, all rounded to 4 decimal places.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE prescriptions (rx_id INT PRIMARY KEY, patient_id VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, drug_class VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, fill_date DATE NOT NULL, days_supply INT NOT NULL);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO prescriptions (rx_id, patient_id, drug_class, fill_date, days_supply) VALUES (1, 'P001', 'oral contraceptives', '2024-01-01', 30), (2, 'P001', 'oral contraceptives', '2024-01-20', 30), (3, 'P002', 'GLP-1 agonists', '2024-01-01', 30), (4, 'P002', 'GLP-1 agonists', '2024-02-15', 30), (5, 'P003', 'statins', '2024-01-01', 90), (6, 'P003', 'statins', '2024-03-25', 90), (7, 'P004', 'SSRIs', '2024-01-01', 30);

composite_moves: compute first fill per patient using MIN(fill_date) grouped by patient_id
flag each patient for refill within each window using CASE expressions
aggregate flags across all patients using SUM and COUNT
compute rates by dividing distinct refilled counts by total patient count

hints: Start by identifying each patient's first fill date.
For each patient, check if any of their fills (excluding the first) fall within 30, 60, or 90 days of their first fill.
Use CASE expressions with date arithmetic to flag patients who refilled within each window, then aggregate those flags across all patients and divide by the total patient count.
problem.answer_key: WITH first_fills AS (SELECT patient_id, MIN(fill_date) AS first_fill_date FROM prescriptions GROUP BY patient_id), refilled_within AS (SELECT ff.patient_id, MAX(CASE WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '30 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS r30, MAX(CASE WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '60 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS r60, MAX(CASE WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '90 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS r90 FROM first_fills ff LEFT JOIN prescriptions p ON p.patient_id = ff.patient_id GROUP BY ff.patient_id) SELECT ROUND(SUM(r30)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_30d, ROUND(SUM(r60)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_60d, ROUND(SUM(r90)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_90d FROM refilled_within;

glossary.definition: The earliest prescription fill date for a given patient, marking the start of their treatment journey.
Any subsequent prescription fill after the first fill for the same patient, indicating continued therapy adherence.
The proportion of patients who obtained at least one refill within a specified time window after their first fill.
The percentage of patients from an initial group who continue engaging with a service or treatment over defined time intervals.
The number of days' worth of medication dispensed in a single prescription fill, typically 30, 60, or 90 days.
The degree to which a patient follows their prescribed medication regimen, often measured by refill timing and consistency.

problem.calculation_explanation: 1. For each patient, find their first fill date by taking the minimum fill_date across all their prescriptions. 2. For each patient, check whether any of their fills (other than the first) occurred within 30, 60, or 90 days after their first fill. 3. Mark each patient with a 1 or 0 for each time window depending on whether they refilled within that window. 4. Sum these flags across all patients to count how many refilled within each window, then divide by the total number of patients to compute each refill rate. 5. Round the results to four decimal places for reporting.

_meta.scenario: a hormone health test kit subscription tracking adherence to repeat-test cadence

user_solution:
WITH first_fills AS (
  -- one row per patient with their first fill date
  SELECT
    patient_id,
    MIN(fill_date) AS first_fill_date
  FROM prescriptions
  GROUP BY patient_id
),
patient_refilled AS (
  -- one row per patient with a 0/1 flag for each window
  -- MAX collapses to one row per patient even if they refilled multiple times in the window
  SELECT
    ff.patient_id,
    MAX(CASE
      WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date
       AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '30 days'
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END) AS r30,
    MAX(CASE
      WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date
       AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '60 days'
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END) AS r60,
    MAX(CASE
      WHEN p.fill_date > ff.first_fill_date
       AND p.fill_date <= ff.first_fill_date + INTERVAL '90 days'
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END) AS r90
  FROM first_fills ff
  LEFT JOIN prescriptions p ON p.patient_id = ff.patient_id
  GROUP BY ff.patient_id
)
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(r30)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_30d,
  ROUND(SUM(r60)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_60d,
  ROUND(SUM(r90)::numeric / COUNT(*), 4) AS refill_rate_90d
FROM patient_refilled;
